title: cospi
summary: Compute cos(X*pi) accurately with exact integer and half-integer results.

gpu_support.notes: GPU inputs gather to the exact host reference path and the floating result is restored to the owning provider.

fusion.notes: Fusion is intentionally disabled because lowering to `cos(X*pi)` would lose the exactness guarantees that distinguish `cospi` from `cos`.

description: `cospi(X)` computes `cos(X*pi)` without first materializing the approximate floating-point product. MATLAB documents single and double real or complex arrays; RunMat mode additionally admits typed integers, logicals, and characters through explicit compatibility gates.
behaviors: Operates element-wise on scalars, vectors, matrices, and N-D tensors.
Single real and complex inputs preserve single output; double inputs preserve double output.
Typed integers are a RunMat-only extension. All eight real integer classes produce double, with exact `+1` or `-1` computed directly from native parity even above `flintmax`.
Logical and character inputs are separately gated RunMat-only extensions and produce double output.
Returns exactly 0 for odd half-integer inputs and exactly ±1 for integer inputs.
Complex inputs use the analytic extension of `cos(pi*z)` while preserving exact real-axis sine/cosine factors when possible.
Output shape matches the input shape; non-finite real inputs produce `NaN`.
String inputs are unsupported and raise a builtin-scoped error.
Table, timetable, tall, and distributed container inputs remain general RunMat container/runtime gaps rather than integer-storage gaps.

examples.description: Avoid floating-point drift at half-integer multiples

faqs.question: Why use `cospi(X)` instead of `cos(X*pi)`?
faqs.answer: `pi` is not exactly representable in binary floating point. `cospi` short-circuits integer and half-integer multiples so common exact results do not contain small rounding noise.

faqs.question: Does `cospi` support gpuArray inputs?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat gathers gpuArray inputs, evaluates the exact host implementation, and restores the result to the owning provider.
